answer: Residency-Weighted Task Lottery. Each identity earns task access only through verified, time-stamped contributions tied to a physical or network location; a "velvet" grace period lets newcomers build history slowly. Duplicate agents on the same island of infrastructure share one access pool, so clones dilute rather than multiply yield. The garden of eligible tasks grows only with proven diversity of execution paths. A marginal clone thus pays onboarding compute plus lost shared rewards, yielding strictly negative expected value.
